name: Habitica
description: Habitica is a task-management app that turns everyday habits, recurring dailies, to-dos, and personal rewards into a role-playing game. People use it to build routines, track goals, level an avatar, earn equipment and pets, and stay accountable through parties, quests, challenges, and community features.
agentUseSummary: Add your Habitica User ID and API token once, then select which agents can read or manage the Habitica account under Safe or Dangerous policy.

credentialRequirements.name: HABITICA_USER_ID
credentialRequirements.label: Habitica User ID
credentialRequirements.helpText: In Habitica, open Settings > API and copy your User ID.

credentialRequirements.name: HABITICA_API_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: Habitica API token
credentialRequirements.helpText: In Habitica, open Settings > API and copy your API token. Treat it like a password.

capabilities.label: Read Habitica progress
capabilities.description: Read authorized habits, dailies, to-dos, rewards, tags, user progress, parties, groups, challenges, quests, chat, notifications, shops, content, and world state.

capabilities.label: Manage Habitica progress
capabilities.description: Create and score tasks, manage tags and account preferences, participate in parties, challenges, quests, chat and shops, and use documented third-party V3 mutations permitted by the account.

allowed.label: Read Habitica
allowed.description: Run one bounded GET request against Habitica's documented third-party V3 API.

approvalRequired.label: Manage Habitica
approvalRequired.description: Run one bounded POST, PUT, or DELETE request; Safe mode requires approval.

blocked.label: Expose credentials
blocked.description: The User ID and API token never enter agent-visible requests, URLs, or results.

blocked.label: Use another origin
blocked.description: Every request is pinned to Habitica's official HTTPS V3 API origin.

blocked.label: Call an internal API family
blocked.description: Authentication, administration, debugging, and official-client payment routes are excluded from the third-party connector.

blocked.label: Run an unbounded transfer
blocked.description: Relay bounds paths, queries, bodies, redirects, results, nesting, and execution time.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Bounded reads run directly. Every task score, creation, update, purchase, message, membership, account change, or deletion requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected token-authorized Habitica operation runs without Relay per-action approval. Connection ownership, provider authority, fixed origin, request bounds, credential protection, provider limits, and audits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts separate bounded read and manage tools and attaches the encrypted User ID and API token only at Habitica's fixed V3 API origin.

providerSetup.blocker: A Habitica user must supply the User ID and API token shown in their own Settings > API page. Habitica's current third-party API uses user-owned header credentials and does not publish a distributable OAuth application flow for Relay to own.
providerSetup.nextAction: Copy the User ID and API token from Habitica Settings > API, connect them in Relay Console, then verify credential health, representative reads, Safe manage approval, Dangerous task scoring and management, redaction, token reset, disconnect, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Habitica's official V3 API documentation publishes its supported task, tag, user, party, group, challenge, quest, chat, notification, shop, content, and world routes.
Habitica's official server source authenticates third-party requests with x-api-user and x-api-key headers and records non-official x-client use.
Habitica's maintained API guide directs third-party tools to V3 and explains that users obtain their User ID and API token from Settings > API.
Habitica describes its gamified tasks, habits, dailies, to-dos, parties, challenges, rewards, and avatar progression.
